description_full: Ellomay Capital Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the initiation, development, construction, and production of renewable and clean energy projects in Europe, the United States, and Israel. The company owns photovoltaic (PV) plants comprising five PV plants in Spain. It also engages in the operation of a dual-fuel operated power plant in Ashkelon, Israel; and construction of a hydro power plant in the Manara Cliff, Israel. In addition, it operates anaerobic digestion plants. The company was formerly known as NUR Macroprinters Ltd. and changed its name to Ellomay Capital Ltd. in April 2008. The company was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel.

financial_summary: Ellomay Capital Ltd is a micro-cap utilities business with a $248M market cap on $44M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 26%.
The company is burning through $70M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 75% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
